reason: The item's own rationale says the Cochrane review (Lima 2004) judged the data insufficient to recommend beta-blockers. The 2024 JAMA Netw Open NMA ranks mirtazapine, biperiden and B6 above propranolol, and propranolol's effect was not robust. The 2026 Schizophr Bull NMA puts 5-HT2A antagonists above beta-blockers, both at low certainty. Downgraded to Moderate: propranolol stays a reasonable conventional first-line add-on, so the defect is the mis-cited evidence and the self-contradiction, not the action. The stem ('strongest evidence as first-line'), the pearl ('strongest evidence') and the evidence line repeat the claim and need the same fix.
evidence: Gerolymos C et al., JAMA Netw Open 2024;7:e241527 (PMID 38451521, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.1527); Furukawa Y et al., Schizophr Bull 2026;52(2) (PMID 38869177, doi:10.1093/schbul/sbae098); Lima AR et al., Cochrane CD001946 (recall, and quoted in the item's rationale)
correction: Propranolol 20–40 mg BID — a lipophilic non-selective beta-blocker and the conventional first-line add-on for akathisia, although its trial evidence is small and low-certainty.

reason: DSM-5-TR's 'with mixed features' specifier for a major depressive episode needs ≥3 of: elevated mood, grandiosity, pressured speech, racing thoughts/flight of ideas, increased energy or goal-directed activity, risky activities, and decreased need for sleep. Overlapping symptoms (psychomotor agitation, insomnia) are not counted. As written, the stem meets only one criterion. Downgraded to Moderate: the keyed action (heightened suicide vigilance) is correct whatever the specifier. The pearl ('racing thoughts/agitation/decreased sleep') and the t_mood.md evidence line ('activation/agitation') carry the same conflation.
evidence: DSM-5-TR (APA 2022), depressive disorders, 'With mixed features' specifier (recall)
correction: he also has racing thoughts, pressured speech, and increased goal-directed activity, and is sleeping only 3 hours per night yet feels rested
